Looker

Announcement

Beginning October 5, 2026, the following features will be automatically enabled for Looker (original) instances running Looker 26.18. Feature enablement for Looker (Google Cloud core) will be announced separately.

Feature

Looker now includes built-in support for the Dremio 26.0+ (Arrow Flight SQL) dialect. The Dremio 26.0+ (Arrow Flight SQL) uses the bundled Apache Arrow Flight SQL JDBC driver, so that you don't have to install unpackaged custom JDBC driver JAR files. See the Dremio documentation page for more information.

Feature

The AI-Assisted Quick Starts feature, called Starter questions in the new Explore experience, is now generally available.

Feature

The new Diagnose & Repair tool evaluates your LookML project repository across eight diagnostic test checks in either your personal development environment or the shared production environment. When issues are found, Looker can automatically perform repairs (such as removing stale lock files, fixing file permissions, or repairing corrupted object indexes) or rebuild damaged repositories while safeguarding uncommitted changes on a dedicated recovery branch.

Feature

Looker Continuous Integration (CI) now includes the Style Validator, which enforces LookML coding standards, naming conventions, and structural best practices across your LookML project. You can run the Style Validator with the default built-in ruleset or customize rule severities, file exclusions, path overrides, and custom rules by adding an lkmlstyle.yaml configuration file to your project repository.

Feature

Now available in preview, Conversational Analytics agentic workflows support scheduled agentic workflows in addition to triggered agentic workflows. You can use scheduled agentic workflows to schedule recurring deliveries of AI-generated insights summaries, data tables, visualizations, and PDF reports to email or Slack by using natural language. Recipients can select Investigate in a workflow notification to open a private, persistent conversation with the data agent.

Users and admins can manage workflows on the updated Manage Workflows user page and Manage Workflows admin page, respectively, and Looker admins can monitor scheduled workflow runs and troubleshoot errors on the new Workflow Executions admin page.

Workflows that were created in versions earlier than Looker 26.14 appear on the Legacy Workflows tab and must be recreated.

Feature

Now available in preview, Looker Data Apps are freeform canvas dashboards that are built by local AI coding agents, such as Gemini CLI, Claude Code, or Cursor, from natural-language prompts. Data Apps give you complete visual layout control (including absolute positioning, overlapping elements, and custom web components) while remaining bound to Looker's governed LookML semantic layer and user permissions.

Change

In Conversational Analytics, the default question mode is now Fast rather than Thinking. Fast mode is intended for answering quickly, and it directly maps your query to underlying LookML definitions without generating reasoning steps. You can still select Thinking mode from the question mode drop-down menu when asking complex, multi-step analytical questions about Explores or dashboards.

Change

The Modern User Interface preview feature toggle now defaults to ON.

Change

The Modern visualization theme now supports map charts (static map points and regions), word cloud charts, and donut multiples. While support for donut multiples was previously documented, it is now officially available with this release. These additions expand the range of visualization options that are available with the modern theme.

Feature

Looker now supports connections to the ClickHouse 26+ dialect. ClickHouse 26+ uses modernized JDBC drivers and introduces support for symmetric aggregates. See the ClickHouse documentation page for more information.

Feature

Enhanced observability metrics, including user engagement and estimated token usage data on the Token usage tab of the Conversational Analytics System Activity dashboard, are now generally available (GA). This launch also adds a Daily Token Utilization visualization and supports token usage observability for Conversational Analytics data agents that are published to Gemini Enterprise. (Note: This item was added on October 20, 2026.)

Model Armor

Feature

Model Armor includes enhanced prompt injection and jailbreak protection for Workspace data. This capability improves detection accuracy and minimizes false positives when screening Workspace content, such as emails, documents, and files.

This capability is available on multi-region endpoints in the US (us) and EU (eu) for templates and floor setting configured with filter version v3 or later, including the Stable and Latest aliases.

Secure Web Proxy

Feature

Secure Web Proxy supports global access. You can enable this feature when creating a Secure Web Proxy instance to make sure that clients from any Google Cloud region can connect to your proxy.

With global access, you can route your outbound traffic through specific regions to meet regulatory compliance or cost requirements. You can also use this option to simplify your network administration by managing outbound traffic from a centralized location.

This feature is available in Preview.

Security Command Center

Feature

Using gcloud CLI, the securitycenter REST API, or client libraries, you can configure Pub/Sub and BigQuery continuous export to receive notifications when findings are deleted from Security Command Center due to data retention policies.

For more information, see the following:

  • Enable finding notifications for Pub/Sub
  • Stream findings to BigQuery for analysis
  • Enable real-time notifications
  • Creating and managing Notification Configs

Sensitive Data Protection

Change

If you set InfoType.version to legacy when including the MEDICAL_ID infoType in your InspectConfig, Sensitive Data Protection now includes MEDICAL_RECORD_NUMBER findings as type MEDICAL_ID in the scan results.

You can now use regular expressions (regex) matchers to configure more flexible and precise traffic routing rules within URL maps for Application Load Balancers. This feature allows you to leverage the power of RE2 syntax for matching on:

  • HTTP Headers: Using the regexMatch field within headerMatches in routeRules.

CodeMender updates (v0.14.0)

This release introduces updates to CodeMender:

  • Better pull request scans: cm find --diff now catches removed security controls and gives large files more time (configurable with --diff-job-timeout).
  • Unified sessions: --deep and --diff scans now appear as a single session in cm session list, cm report, and cm stats.
  • Moved code in cm verify: cm verify now finds code that moved since cm find and updates the finding's location.
  • Guided activation: cm now opens the activation page and waits for activation instead of exiting.
  • New cm find flags: --deep-max-turns limits exploratory steps per file in --deep scans, and --enable-bash allows shell commands during scans.
  • Improved detection: More distinct findings per file and more precise CWE classification for weak hashing and randomness.
  • Bug fixes:
    • Fixed scans of repositories reached through nested symbolic links.
    • Fixed findings for nonexistent files and over-merged findings.
    • Shell scripts created by cm verify are now executable.

For more information, see the CodeMender documentation.

Fixed

The following issues were fixed in 1.35.600-gke.140:

  • Fixed vulnerabilities listed in Vulnerability fixes.
  • Fixed an issue where audit-proxy retried audit log exports indefinitely on permanent errors, generating excessive audit logging traffic.
  • Fixed an issue where the Kubernetes preflight health check scanned all namespaces in the admin cluster instead of the target cluster's namespace, causing cluster upgrades to fail if an unrelated cluster had stale reconciling resources.
  • Fixed an issue where user clusters repeatedly alternated between reconciling and running states if the management cluster configured a different pod density configuration than the user cluster.

Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for bare metal

Announcement

Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for bare metal 1.35.600-gke.140 is now available for download. To upgrade, see Upgrade clusters. Google Distributed Cloud for bare metal 1.35.600-gke.140 runs on Kubernetes v1.35.8-gke.100.

After a release, it takes approximately 7 to 14 days for the version to become available for installations or upgrades with the GKE On-Prem API clients: the Google Cloud console, the gcloud CLI, and Terraform.

If you use a third-party storage vendor, check the listing of our previously-qualified storage partners.

Fixed

The following issues were fixed in 1.35.600-gke.140:

  • Fixed vulnerabilities listed in Vulnerability fixes.
  • Improved containerd resilience against state corruption if a node reboots while unpacking container images.
  • Fixed an issue where the periodic configuration drift health check failed with a version not supported error while a cluster upgrade or rollback was in progress.
  • Fixed an issue where audit-proxy retried audit log exports indefinitely on permanent errors, generating excessive audit logging traffic.
  • Fixed an issue where the Kubernetes preflight health check scanned all namespaces in the admin cluster instead of the target cluster's namespace, causing cluster upgrades to fail if an unrelated cluster had stale reconciling resources.
  • Fixed an issue where upgrading or recreating a node during maintenance mode could proceed before storage volumes finished detaching, resulting in orphaned CSI VolumeAttachment resources or I/O errors. After the fix, node drain verifies that kubelet unmounts all host volumes and that CSI VolumeAttachment resources detach before completing the drain.
  • Fixed an issue where Certificate Authority (CA) rotation failed for self-managing clusters (admin, hybrid, and standalone). The failure occurs during the final phase of the rotation when attempting to move management resources back from the temporary bootstrap cluster to the self-managing cluster, which can leave the cluster in an unmanageable state. You must upgrade your clusters to version 1.35.600-gke.140 before you rotate your CAs.
  • Fixed an issue where BareMetalMachine status conditions prematurely reported nodes as ready and available during maintenance mode transitions.
  • Fixed an issue in clusters using bundled BGP load balancing where control plane upgrades or configuration updates could cause up to 20 seconds of API server connection failures while a control plane node restarted. After the fix, failover to a healthy control plane node completes in approximately 4 seconds.
  • Fixed an issue where user clusters repeatedly alternated between reconciling and running states if the management cluster configured a different pod density configuration than the user cluster.

Feature

[Spotlight Feature] Monitor response and playbook health with the Response Health Hub

Google SecOps now includes the Response Health Hub curated dashboard, a central location for monitoring playbook performance, execution latency, automation effectiveness, and integration health across environments.

Key capabilities include:

  • Volume and adoption tracking: Monitor total playbook execution volume, daily trends, completion success rates, and queued playbook backlogs.
  • Attachment and rerun insights: Track average and maximum playbooks attached per case or alert, and identify playbooks with high rerun counts.
  • Execution latency diagnostics: Compare end-to-end playbook execution time against active action execution time, and drill down into the 30 slowest playbook and action runs.
  • Playbook and integration health monitoring: Investigate the latest failed playbook runs, highest failure-rate and terminated playbooks, and integration action error reasons.
  • Automation effectiveness metrics: Compare automated versus manual case closure rates and Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR).

For more information, see Monitor response and playbook health.

Spend cap budgets are now generally available for a limited set of services

For eligible services, you can configure a spend cap budget to automatically pause usage when your estimated spend exceeds the budget amount you set. You can manage spend cap budgets in the Budgets page in the Google Cloud console and using the Cloud Billing Budget API.

Spend caps are a cost control mechanism. A spend cap is enforced when usage costs exceed your budget target amount. When enforced, any new request to the eligible services, within the specified project, are paused and no further usage costs are accrued until the spend cap is lifted. You can manually lift an enforced spend cap, or wait until the start of the next month when the spend cap is automatically lifted.

Spend caps use gross, estimated costs to trigger the alerts and caps, enforcing a cap much faster than the actual costs are processed and appear on billing reports. Even though faster than reports, the enforcement of spend caps isn't instant and any cost overages are billed as normal.

More information about spend cap budgets

For managing spend cap budgets in the Google Cloud console, see:

  • Lift an enforced spend cap

For managing spend cap budgets using the Cloud Billing Budget API, see:

Certificate Manager

Change

Google-managed public SSL certificates signed by Google Public CA (pki.goog) are gradually transitioning from a 90-day validity period to a 45-day validity period to improve security.

To align with modern industry-wide security standards and promote shorter certificate lifespans, Google-managed public certificates now rotate more frequently. This proactive rotation enhances the overall security posture of load balancers. The transition requires no manual intervention or configuration changes as Certificate Manager automatically manages both issuance and renewal.

For more information, see Google-managed certificates and Use Google-managed certificates.

Cloud Load Balancing

Change

Google-managed public SSL certificates signed by Public Certificate Authority (pki.goog) are gradually transitioning from a 90-day validity period to a 45-day validity period to improve security.

To align with modern industry-wide security standards and promote shorter certificate lifespans, Google-managed public certificates signed by Public Certificate Authority now rotate more frequently.

This proactive rotation enhances the overall security posture of load balancers. Transition requires no manual intervention or configuration changes as Google Cloud automatically manages issuance and renewal for both Certificate Manager and Compute Engine SSL certificates.

For more information, see Renew a Google-managed SSL certificate.

Service rate limiting policies are now available in Preview for regional internal Application Load Balancers and Secure Web Proxies.

Service rate limiting policies let you maintain service availability among trusted clients that might consume an inordinate amount of resources.

Secure Web Proxy supports service rate limiting policies. Use these policies to protect external destinations from traffic overloads and manage the costs of your outbound web traffic.

title: October 15, 2026
description:
Apigee Edge for Private Cloud

Announcement

Released Apigee Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.

Designated Apigee Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.00 a long-term support (LTS) release: 18 months of full support ending April 2028, then 18 months of maintenance ending October 2029. After October 2029, 4.54.00.00 receives no software updates, security mitigations, or technical support.

Installing a later 4.54 minor release or patch does not change those dates. To extend the support lifecycle, upgrade to the next LTS release.

For the support lifecycle phases, release cadences, and version numbering, see Apigee Edge for Private Cloud release and lifecycle policy.

Announcement

This release replaces Java 8 with Java 17 and Java 21, removes the Classic UI and the apigee-sso component, and updates the bundled Cassandra, Postgres, OpenLDAP, ZooKeeper, Qpid Broker-J, Nginx, and Consul versions. These changes are not backward-compatible.

For the 4.54.00 versions and the 4.53.01 versions they replace, see Supported software and supported versions.

Before upgrading, read Changes in Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00, then Update Apigee Edge 4.53.00 or 4.53.01 to 4.54.00 or New installation overview. For known issues, see Known issues with Edge for Private Cloud.

Announcement

Replaced the Classic UI (edge-ui) with the New Edge UI (edge-management-ui).

The New Edge UI is the only management UI in 4.54.00 and is installed by default. Deployments running the Classic UI must transition to it before upgrading. Custom Classic UI properties do not carry over automatically. The default port also changes from 9000 to 3001, configurable with conf_uebe_port, so firewall rules and load balancer target ports that point at 9000 fail until they are updated.

For the migration steps and the supported feature list, see Migrate to the New Edge UI and What features are supported?.

Breaking

In deployments with Apigee SSO enabled, an integrated OIDC identity broker in apigee-openldap replaces the standalone apigee-sso component and Apache Tomcat 9.0.x. Before upgrading, take a complete and validated LDAP backup; existing apigee-sso configurations do not migrate automatically. Deployments not using Apigee SSO require no action.

For migration prerequisites, validation checks, and rollback constraints, see Option 2: Upgrade UI (with Apigee SSO).

Breaking

4.54.00 runs Java in mixed mode: Java 17 for Cassandra and ZooKeeper, Java 21 for the Management Server, Message Processor, Router, and Qpid Broker-J. Both Oracle JDK and OpenJDK are supported at those versions.

Oracle JDK 8 and OpenJDK 8 are no longer supported.

API proxies with custom JavaCallout policies or custom resource JARs can break on Java 21. For details, see Changes in Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.

Change

Upgraded Nginx on the Edge Router to 1.30.0.

If you are upgrading from Nginx 1.20.x, see Nginx 1.30 changes in Apigee Edge 4.54.00 for the full list of changes.

Change

Changed the TLS defaults on Message Processors to the Java 21 cryptographic baseline.

Message Processors run on Java 21, which enables TLS 1.3 by default (JEP 332) and prefers it for outbound backend connections, falling back to TLS 1.2. No configuration change is required if your target servers and load balancers negotiate TLS 1.3, or negotiate TLS 1.2 with forward-secret (ECDHE) cipher suites.

Java 21 also disables the non-forward-secret static RSA key-exchange suites (TLS_RSA_*). If you have overridden conf_http_HTTPTransport.ssl.cipher.suites.whitelist or conf_message-processor-communication_local.http.ssl.ciphers with static RSA suites only, backend calls fail with no cipher suites in common and the Router cannot complete a TLS handshake with the Message Processor. Replace the TLS_RSA_* entries with modern cipher suites and restart the Message Processor.

For the remediation path, see Legacy backend requirements and remediation.

Feature

Added Basic authentication to the New Edge UI, which lets you sign in without configuring an identity provider.

The New Edge UI supports Basic authentication without additional configuration. You can also configure Apigee SSO, or an external identity provider such as SAML or OIDC. This feature is generally available in 4.54.00.

Feature

Added automated pre-flight validation checks to apigee-setup and apigee-service, which surface environment configuration problems before a component is installed.

This feature is generally available in 4.54.00.

Security

Fixed multiple security vulnerabilities in Apigee Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.

These fixes ship as part of the component upgrades in this release; see Changes in Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.

Change

Changed the default garbage collector on Message Processors to the Garbage-First garbage collector.

Message Processors set useG1GC=true and useStringDeduplication=true by default in 4.54.00. In 4.53.01 neither was set by default. To configure garbage collection, see Configure the garbage collector for Message Processors.

Apigee Edge for Public Cloud

Announcement

On October 15, 2026, we began releasing Single Sign-On (SSO) updates for Apigee Edge for Public Cloud.

Fixed

Bug ID Component Description
560310696 SSO Fixed an issue where the Portal SSO endpoint inadvertently accepted deprecated TLS 1.1 connections. The endpoint now strictly enforces TLS 1.2+.

Apigee Integrated Portal

Announcement

On October 15, 2026, we released a new version of the Apigee integrated portal.

Fixed

Bug ID Description
560310696 Fixed an issue where the Portal SSO endpoint inadvertently accepted deprecated TLS 1.1 connections. The endpoint now strictly enforces TLS 1.2+.

Apigee X

Fixed

Bug ID Description
466116259 Updated the startup script for the managed instance group (MIG) that routes external traffic to Apigee. net.ipv4.ip_forward is now written to /etc/sysctl.d/, so an instance no longer stops forwarding traffic when a reboot or an OS update resets it. The script does not change unrelated iptables NAT rules. Instances pick up the change the next time they are restarted or recreated.

BigQuery

Feature

You can copy tables across regions. This feature is now generally available (GA).

Feature

You can now use reusable column aliases in GoogleSQL. This feature lets you define an alias for an expression in the SELECT clause of a SQL query and immediately reference that alias within the same SELECT list or in the WHERE clause of the same query block.

Reusable column aliases also streamline the migration of workloads from other data warehouses such as Snowflake and Teradata, by supporting their syntax.

This feature is generally available, and is opt-in only. To use reusable column aliases, you must first enable the feature.

Feature

You can export a conversational analytics agent's answer, including text, visualizations, tables, and citations, to a PDF or CSV file. This feature is generally available (GA).

Cloud Vision

Deprecated

Face detection model update

The emotion label response in the Cloud Vision API is deprecated. Going forward, the Cloud Vision API face detection (FACE_DETECTION feature) will return UNKNOWN for all emotion-related labels.

Compute Engine

Feature

Preview: You can create regional disks, including Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability volumes, by cloning a zonal boot disk.

For more information, see Duplicate a disk with clones.

Change

If you try to create an on-demand reservation or increase the number of reserved Compute Engine instances in a reservation when the zone has reached its reservation capacity limit for your requested machine family, then the request fails with a RESERVATION_CAPACITY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED error. For more information, see Reservation capacity limit exceeded.

Feature

Generally available: The storage-optimized Z4M machine series is generally available for Compute Engine. Powered by fifth generation Intel Emerald Rapids Xeon Scalable processors and Titanium offload processors, Z4M instances are purpose-built for workloads that require larger storage capacity, such as:

  • Parallel file systems to support AI/ML workloads
  • I/O intensive workloads such as SQL, NoSQL, and vector databases
  • AI/ML training and inference workloads such as checkpointing and distributed Key-Value (KV) cache

The Z4M machine series delivers up to 1,536 GB of memory and 168,000 GiB of local Titanium SSD capacity. Z4M also supports up to 400 Gbps of network bandwidth using two physical NICs. Z4M instances use Titanium and Cloud RDMA to help enable higher levels of networking performance, isolation, and security.

For more information, see Storage-optimized machine family.

Dataflow

Feature

Dataflow Auto VM Selection now supports 4th generation Compute Engine machine series. When Auto VM Selection is enabled, the service prioritizes these newer generation VMs for improved performance. If 4th generation VMs are unavailable at startup, the service automatically falls back to widely available 2nd generation machine families to ensure that your jobs can start without unnecessary delays.

For more information, see Auto VM Selection.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Anthropic models are available in the Gemini Enterprise app

Administrators can make Anthropic models—Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5—available to users in the Gemini Enterprise app. After an administrator turns on a model in the Enable third-party models section of the Feature Management tab, users can select the model in the model selector. Claude models are available in the global location and the us and eu multi-regions, and are charged on a pay-as-you-go basis.

This feature is generally available. For more information, see Enable third-party models.

Looker

Announcement

The latest versions in the Looker (Google Cloud core) release channels are beginning deployment as follows:

  • Latest version in the Rapid channel: Looker 26.20
  • Latest version in the No Channel channel: Looker 26.20

The latest version in the Regular channel remains Looker 26.18.

Note: This item was added on October 23, 2026.

Feature

The Looker 26.18 features have begun to be enabled for Looker (Google Cloud core) instances.

NetApp Volumes

Announcement

Google Cloud NetApp Volumes now supports the Flex Unified service level, including custom performance, in the following region:

  • europe-west8 (Milan)

For more information about available regions, see Supported regions.

Security Command Center

Feature

To increase the precision of attack path analysis and provide attack exposure scores that help you prioritize confirmed internet exposures, Risk Engine attack path simulations support the EXTERNALLY_EXPOSED_VM_INSTANCE External Exposure finding category (Preview). This finding category identifies Compute Engine or Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) resources with a direct public IP address that allows host OS access.

For more information, see Detect exposed resources, Risk Engine feature support, and Overview of attack exposure scores and attack paths.

Video Intelligence API

Deprecated

We are deprecating the emotion label response in the API. Going forward, the API will return UNKNOWN for all emotion related labels.

title: October 20, 2026
description:
Agent Platform Workbench

Change

M154 Release

Change

Installed latest packages from upstream dependencies.

Fixed

Fixed dataset and table search in the BigQuery panel, which sometimes failed to return results. Root cause is due to Datacatalog API being sunsetted in favor of Dataplex API.

Apigee X

Announcement

On October 20th, 2026, we began maintenance updates of Apigee instances configured for maintenance windows.

If you set a preferred window for maintenance for your instance, and your instance version is below 1-18-0-apigee-6, your instance will be updated to 1-18-0-apigee-6 within the next seven to 21 days. A notification containing the expected date of upgrade will be sent within the next two business days.

Note: Instances that meet either of the following two criteria will not be updated:
  • Your instance has a DNS misconfiguration, as described in Known Issue 445936920.
  • Your instance uses an Apigee Java Library that has been removed, as described in Apigee release notes dated October 16, 2025.

For more information on participating in scheduled maintenance windows, see Maintenance overview and Manage Apigee instance maintenance windows.

Cloud Workstations

Feature

Cloud Workstations supports automatic failover for boost configurations in Preview. When you enable automatic failover, Cloud Workstations automatically provisions a workstation VM using the boost configuration if Compute Engine lacks capacity for the default machine type during startup.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Antigravity Enterprise Gateway support

Antigravity Enterprise Gateway lets organizations route model inference requests from the Antigravity app, Antigravity CLI, and Antigravity for IDEs through a centralized enterprise gateway before forwarding them to Google Cloud. This deployment enables organizations to inspect and audit model traffic, enforce custom security and network egress policies, and authenticate developers through a gateway API key without requiring individual Google Account sign-in.

Requests routed through Antigravity Enterprise Gateway use a centralized Google Cloud service account and are billed on a pay-as-you-go (PAYG) consumption basis through the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. This deployment model doesn't use your Gemini Enterprise seat-based subscription quotas (such as included Standard or Plus monthly allowances). You can't use a gateway and sign in with a Google Account at the same time. If you want to use your included subscription quota instead, disable the enterprise gateway and sign in with your Google Account.

This feature is generally available (GA).

For more information, see:

  • Deploy Antigravity Enterprise Gateway
  • Connect Antigravity to an Enterprise Gateway.

Breaking

Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 2.5 Pro discontinued in Canada and Japan

Gemini 2.5 Pro has been discontinued for in-country Gemini Enterprise app deployments in Canada and Japan. Agents and chat sessions in these regions that previously used Gemini 2.5 Pro automatically switch to in-country Gemini 3.5 Flash.

Gemini 2.5 Pro remains available in the global, us, and eu regions.

For more information, see Data residency for Gemini Enterprise and Manage web app features.

Google Kubernetes Engine

Fixed

A security issue in GKE fleet management that could have allowed unauthorized configuration changes to clusters registered to a fleet has been resolved. The fixes are rolled out to all regions, and no action is required.

Fixed

This is an update to the release note regarding the Cloud Storage FUSE CSI driver issue published on October 2, 2026.

This issue has been resolved. You can upgrade your cluster control plane to the following versions to fix the issue for ubuntu_containerd and older cos_containerd node pools:

  • 1.36.5-gke.1032000 or later

  • 1.37.1-gke.1552000 or later

  • Specific 1.36.4 mitigation patches: 1.36.4-gke.1247001, 1.36.4-gke.1247002, 1.36.4-gke.1391001, 1.36.4-gke.1391003, 1.36.4-gke.1495001, 1.36.4-gke.1495003, 1.36.4-gke.2046001, 1.36.4-gke.2202002

Looker

Announcement

The latest versions in the Looker (Google Cloud core) release channels are beginning deployment as follows:

  • Latest version in the Regular channel: Looker 26.18

The latest version in the Rapid and No Channel channels remains Looker 26.20.

Note: This item was added on October 23, 2026.

Note: This item was updated on October 29, 2026, to correct the latest version in the Regular channel to Looker 26.18.

Managed Service for Apache Airflow

Feature

Upgrade rollbacks are available in Managed Airflow (Gen 3). You can roll back an environment upgrade if you encounter degraded performance, Airflow bugs, or compatibility issues with your DAGs, plugins, or dependencies.

This feature is gradually rolling out over several releases. In this release, it's available in the following regions: africa-south1, asia-northeast2, asia-south2, australia-southeast2, europe-north2, europe-southwest1, europe-west10, europe-west12, europe-west8, me-central1, me-central2, me-west1, northamerica-northeast2, northamerica-south1, southamerica-west1, us-south1, asia-east1, asia-northeast3, asia-southeast2, europe-central2, europe-west4, europe-west6, europe-west9, northamerica-northeast1, southamerica-east1, us-east5, us-west3, us-west4, asia-east2, asia-southeast3.

Change

Improved Airflow worker health checks to detect task queue connection issues more quickly.

Change

New Airflow builds are available in Managed Airflow (Gen 3):

  • composer-3-airflow-3.3.1-build.5
  • composer-3-airflow-3.2.2-build.9
  • composer-3-airflow-2.11.1-build.22 (default)

Change

New images are available in Managed Airflow (Gen 2):

  • composer-2.17.16-airflow-2.11.1 (default)

Spanner

Feature

Spanner supports approximate aggregate functions for both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects. These functions produce statistical estimates of distinct counts, allowing you to compute results faster and save resources on large datasets compared to exact aggregation.

For more information, see approximate aggregate functions (GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL), HyperLogLog++ functions, and Sketches.

title: October 21, 2026
description:
Apigee X

Announcement

Apigee Emulator

Apigee Emulator v2.0.2

On October 21, 2026, we released Apigee Emulator version 2.0.2.

This release upgrades the Apigee Emulator runtime to Java 21 (Eclipse Temurin JRE 21) to align local proxy development and policy execution with the production Apigee runtime, while keeping the embedded Apache Cassandra datastore pinned to Java 8. It also addresses 46 security vulnerabilities across Netty, Jackson, Apache Log4j, BouncyCastle, Apache CXF, Eclipse Jetty, and the embedded Cassandra Go standard library health-check binary.

The emulator image is available at Artifact Registry.

To upgrade, update the emulator version in your Cloud Code for VS Code settings to 2.0.2. See Manage the Apigee Emulator for details.

Feature

Apigee Emulator

Changed in this release

  • Upgraded the Apigee Emulator runtime JVM to Eclipse Temurin JRE 21 (21.0.12.1.0+1-0, from JRE 11 11.0.31+11), adding JVM 21 compatibility flags (-Djava.security.manager=allow and --add-opens module flags) for JavaCallout, JavaScript (Rhino), and Python (Jython) policies while keeping the embedded Apache Cassandra 4.0.19 datastore pinned to Eclipse Temurin JRE 8.
  • Upgraded Netty to 4.1.137.Final (from 4.1.135.Final) and updated netty-tcnative-boringssl-static and netty-tcnative-classes to 2.0.81.Final (from 2.0.77.Final).
  • Upgraded Jackson (jackson-core, jackson-databind, and jackson-dataformat-yaml) to 2.21.7 (from 2.18.6 and 2.19.2) and jackson-annotations to 2.21.
  • Upgraded shaded Apache Log4j (log4j-api and log4j-core) in ConfigUtil.jar to 2.25.5 (from 2.17.1 and 2.25.4).
  • Upgraded BouncyCastle (bcprov-jdk18on, bcpkix-jdk18on, and bcutil-jdk18on) to 1.85 (from 1.84).
  • Upgraded Apache CXF (cxf-*) to 3.6.12 (from 3.5.11).
  • Upgraded gRPC to 1.82.3 (from 1.62.2), Protobuf (protobuf-java and protobuf-java-util) to 4.33.6 (from 3.25.5), and Guava to 33.5.0-jre (from 33.4.8-jre).
  • Removed unused org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-* (9.4.58.v20250814) and commons-collections:commons-collections (3.2.2) JARs from the emulator distribution.
  • Refreshed the Cassandra base image to pick up Go standard library 1.27.0 (from 1.25.11) in the embedded /opt/apigee/ready health-check binary.

Announcement

v1.15.9

On October 21, 2026 we released an updated version of the Apigee hybrid software, v1.15.9.

  • For information on upgrading, see Upgrading Apigee hybrid to version v1.15.9.
  • For information on new installations, see The big picture.
Note: This is a patch release: The container images used in patch releases are integrated with the Apigee hybrid Helm charts. Upgrading to a patch via the Helm chart automatically updates the images. No manual image changes are typically needed. For information on container image support in Apigee hybrid releases, see Apigee release process.

Fixed

Bug ID Description
573622417 Fixed an issue where apigee-ingressgateway forwarded the x-envoy-decorator-operation header to upstream runtime and target backends.
571378258 The apigee-redis container now uses the Valkey engine (version 8.1.10). The RESP2 wire protocol and redis-server and redis-cli binary names are unchanged.
568860869 Fixed an issue in the RegularExpressionProtection policy where patterns starting and ending with .* whose middle section contained regular expression syntax were matched as literal text instead of regular expressions.
565072374 Fixed an issue where VerifyJWT policies using a JWKS uriRef could return steps.jwt.NoMatchingPublicKey on the first request after the 5-minute JWKS cache TTL expired when the identity provider rotated keys. The cache now refreshes synchronously upon expiration.
535395491 Extension Processor (ext_proc) denials now return the status and body that the policy or FaultRule produced, instead of always returning HTTP 500.
524115876 Fixed an intermittent HTTP 400 error in the OASValidation policy's strict parameter validation that rejected valid requests under load.
519729209 Fixed a SAML XML Signature Wrapping vulnerability in the ValidateSAMLAssertion policy.
502231886 Fixed an issue where the SanitizeUserPrompt and SanitizeModelResponse policies failed to extract content using default source templates when the <Source> element was omitted and <IgnoreUnresolvedVariables> was set to false.
432315283 Fixed an issue where changes to a multi-certificate truststore's trust anchors required a Message Processor restart when features.truststore.multi_cert_bundle.enabled was toggled at runtime; the outbound SSLContext now rebuilds automatically.
428750492 Removed the required validation constraint on the strategy and stages fields in the ApigeeDeployment CRD.

API Gateway

Deprecated

Negative backend deadlines are deprecated

A negative backend deadline in an OpenAPI 2.0 x-google-backend extension or a gRPC BackendRule uses the default deadline, the same as 0. Negative values there are deprecated and will be rejected in a future release; until then, creating an API config with one returns a warning in the operation metadata. OpenAPI 3.x backends already reject a negative deadline. To use the default, omit the field or set it to 0.

For more information, see OpenAPI 2.0 extensions and OpenAPI 3.x extensions.

Cloud Database Migration Service

Security

On Saturday, October 17, 2026, Google received a report from a security researcher regarding the compromise of private keys associated with eight eMudhra subordinate Certification Authority (CA) certificates, including those cross-signed by AAA Certificate Services. Consequently, these CA certificates are no longer trusted and are being revoked.

To continue connecting to a source database after its CA certificate is updated, upload the new CA certificate to the Database Migration Service source connection profile:

  • Update the connection profile using gcloud database-migration connection-profiles update or the connectionProfiles.patch API method.
  • Modify the connection profile in the Google Cloud console:
    • MySQL connection profiles
    • PostgreSQL to Cloud SQL connection profiles
    • PostgreSQL to AlloyDB for PostgreSQL connection profiles
    • Oracle to Cloud SQL connection profiles
    • Oracle to AlloyDB for PostgreSQL connection profiles
    • SQL Server to Cloud SQL connection profiles
    • SQL Server to AlloyDB for PostgreSQL connection profiles

For more information, see security bulletin GCP-2026-071.

Security

In response to GCP-2026-071, Google is updating Cloud SQL's managed components. No manual updates to the certificate store are required for Cloud SQL-managed instances. The fix is shipping in a new maintenance version that will be applied during scheduled maintenance. You can also apply the fix by performing self-service maintenance. An announcement will be published when the self-service maintenance fix is available.

What should I do?

  • If you use the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy, then upgrade the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy to 2.26.3 or later and the Cloud SQL Proxy Operator to 1.8.4 or later. If you run the standalone proxy binary, then also update the host's certificate authority (CA) certificates.

  • If you use a Cloud SQL Language Connector, then update the language runtime and operating system CA certificates used with the Cloud SQL Language Connector (for example, Go 1.26.10 or 1.27.3 or later, certifi 2026.10.19 or later).

  • If you're using the gcloud CLI to install the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy, then update the gcloud CLI to 590.0.1.

Announcement

Starting November 1, 2026, at 02:00 a.m. local time, unpatched Cloud SQL for MySQL instances that evaluate certain local Canadian time zones (across Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, and Northwest Territories) will lag by one hour because the instances still follow the autumn fall back schedule. Stored timestamp data isn't modified.

What should I do?

Before November 1, 2026, do one of the following fixes:

  • Apply self-service maintenance (Recommended): If your applications rely on database functions to calculate, schedule, or display times in these Canadian time zones (such as Calgary, Edmonton, Vancouver, or Winnipeg), then update your instances to the latest maintenance release using the Google Cloud console or the gcloud CLI.

    Updated time zone rules that reflect permanent standard daylight offsets across Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, and Northwest Territories are supported in Cloud SQL for MySQL maintenance release *.R20260726.00_36 or later.

    For more information, see Perform self-service maintenance.

  • Database configuration stopgap: If your organization can't restart instances before November 1, 2026, then you can set the time zone for your database session without causing downtime for your instance. Set the default_time_zone flag for the database session to your target fixed numeric offset (for example, '-06:00' for Alberta, '-07:00' for British Columbia, or '-05:00' for Manitoba).

    For more information about configuring database flags, see Configure database flags.

Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL

Announcement

Starting November 1, 2026, at 02:00 a.m. local time, unpatched Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instances that evaluate certain local Canadian time zones (across Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, and Northwest Territories) will lag by one hour because the instances still follow the autumn fall back schedule. Stored timestamp data isn't modified.

What should I do?

Before November 1, 2026, do one of the following fixes:

  • Apply self-service maintenance (Recommended): If your applications rely on database functions to calculate, schedule, or display times in these Canadian time zones (such as Calgary, Edmonton, Vancouver, or Winnipeg), then update your instances to the latest maintenance release using the Google Cloud console or the gcloud CLI.

    Updated time zone rules that reflect permanent standard daylight offsets across Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, and Northwest Territories are supported in Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL maintenance release *.R20260712.01_44 or later.

    For more information, see Perform self-service maintenance.

  • Database configuration stopgap: If your organization can't restart instances before November 1, 2026, then you can set your database session time zone without downtime to an anchor zone.

    ALTER DATABASE database_name SET timezone TO 'anchor_zone';

    Replace the following:

    • database_name: the name of your database.

    • anchor_zone: the anchor zone to use as the time zone for your database. Specify an anchor zone that operates on a permanent offset.

      For example, 'America/Regina' for Alberta and Northwest Territories (UTC-6), 'America/Whitehorse' for British Columbia (UTC-7), or 'America/Coral_Harbour' for Manitoba (UTC-5).

Cloud SQL for SQL Server

Announcement

Starting November 1, 2026, at 02:00 a.m. local time, Cloud SQL for SQL Server instances that evaluate certain local Canadian time zones (across Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, and Northwest Territories) will lag by one hour because the instances still follow the autumn fall back schedule. Stored timestamp data isn't modified.

What should I do?

For SQL Server, Microsoft has published guidance, recommending updating each applicable instance's time zone to the Windows time zone with the matching fixed offset.

Update each instance's time zone to the Windows time zone with the matching fixed offset:

Jurisdiction Current time zone Recommended time zone Fixed offset
British Columbia Pacific Standard Time Yukon Standard Time UTC-07:00
Alberta / Inuvik, NWT Mountain Standard Time Canada Central Standard Time UTC-06:00
Manitoba Central Standard Time Eastern Standard Time (Mexico) UTC-05:00

You can make the change in the Google Cloud console (Edit instance > Flags and parameters > Time zone) or with gcloud:

gcloud sql instances patch INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project=PROJECT_ID \
  --time-zone="Yukon Standard Time"

Feature

Gemini Notebook Enterprise: Visual refresh

This update includes the following changes and features. These features are generally available (GA):

  • Refreshed UI design: The user interface features an updated color scheme and style that match the consumer and Google Workspace versions of Gemini Notebook.

  • Audio overview language selection: You can choose the language for the audio overview output. This lets you create an audio output in a language different from the notebook's language (Settings > Output language).

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Feature

Inference request metadata logging (GA)

Inference request metadata logging is generally available. Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform can write one Cloud Logging entry for every inference request your project serves. Each entry records the model, region, consumption option, token counts, Provisioned Throughput usage, latency and error code. Entries record metadata only and never contain prompts or responses. Logging is supported for Gemini models that use generateContent and streamGenerateContent, and for Claude models that use rawPredict and streamRawPredict.

You can turn on logging in the Google Cloud console, from the Provisioned Throughput page, or with the REST API. Turning on logging in the console also turns on detailed metrics, which chart Provisioned Throughput traffic at one-second resolution. With logging on, the model observability dashboard adds 1-second resolution options to its charts for pay-as-you-go traffic. To attribute usage to a team, application or tenant, add request headers with the x-goog-agent-platform-observability-label- prefix, and query the entries with SQL in Observability Analytics.

For more information, see Log inference request metadata.

Computer use tool is available in General Availability

Looker

Announcement

On November 1, 2026, several Canadian provinces and territories—Manitoba, Alberta, British Columbia, and parts of the Northwest Territories—transition to permanent daylight saving time (DST) or remain on their summer UTC offsets year-round. On unpatched Looker instances, these changes affect scheduled content delivery fire times and table calculations that use now() with the affected Canadian time zones (America/Winnipeg, Canada/Central, America/Rainy_River, America/Edmonton, Canada/Mountain, America/Vancouver, Canada/Pacific, and America/Inuvik). Patched Looker builds update the scheduler (Ruby) and browser (JavaScript) time zone data, while server-evaluated now() table calculations on the JVM still use the bundled JDK time zone database (tzdb 2026b). To learn how to upgrade to a patched Looker build or configure an alternative schedule delivery time zone, see 2026 Canadian time zone changes.

Issue

Starting October 24, 2026, Managed Airflow (Gen 3) and Managed Airflow (Gen 2) environments running Python 3.11 with google-api-core package versions 2.28.0 to 2.43.0 (including versions 2.30.3 to 2.43.0, which weren't previously affected) might experience degraded performance because of a Python 3.11 deprecation check that scans installed package metadata on every new Python subprocess import. You might observe increased DAG parsing times, longer task execution times, higher CPU usage on Airflow DAG processors and workers, and frequent FutureWarning log entries from google/api_core/_python_version_support.py about Python 3.11 support ending on 2027-10-24.

For the list of affected builds and available workarounds (installing google-api-core>=2.43.1 on compatible Airflow 3 builds or applying a sitecustomize.py runtime patch), see the known issue for Managed Airflow (Gen 3) or Managed Airflow (Gen 2).

This release includes:

  • Log ingestion from SAP RISE and self-managed SAP environments that run on Google Cloud, on-premises, or other clouds.
  • SAP-specific YARA-L threat detection rules available in the Google SecOps Detection Rules GitHub repository.
  • Automated threat response and containment capabilities by using the SAP RFC Gateway and SOAR playbooks (Preview).

For more information, see Secure SAP applications with Google SecOps.

Spanner

Feature

Spanner supports equality and ordering comparisons on JSONB and JSON values. You can use these values in GROUP_BY and ORDER BY clauses without first converting them to another data type.

In GoogleSQL, you can also convert other data types to JSON using CAST(expression AS JSON) and compare JSON values directly with non-JSON values. Spanner can implicitly coerces the non-JSON value to JSON for comparison.

Additionally, you can use search indexes to accelerate equality comparisons such as = or IN on JSONB and JSON columns and subpaths.

For more information, see JSON comparison and sorting , JSON comparison coercion , CAST AS JSON , JSON search indexes , and Working with JSONB.

Feature

Spanner Graph supports the following enhancements:

  • You can create property graphs from SQL views that call remote functions (Preview) to compute node and edge properties. For more information, see Compute properties with remote functions.
  • You can write simplified queries on schemaless dynamic properties without explicit conversions to SQL data types. This lets you group and sort dynamic properties, and compare them directly with literal values or other dynamic properties. For more information, see Filter, compare, and sort by dynamic properties and JSON comparison and sorting.

Feature

For mutual TLS (mTLS) on Application Load Balancers, frontend mTLS validation relaxations are generally available.

The ALLOW_VALIDATION_RELAXATIONS client validation mode on the Client Authentication (ServerTlsPolicy) resource allows you to configure specific X.509 certificate validation exceptions to standard client certificate validation rules. This simplifies migrations of legacy workloads while maintaining an active security posture.

This mode supports the following client certificate validation relaxation parameters:

  • ALLOW_MISSING_EKU: Bypasses Extended Key Usage validation if the EKU extension is absent in the client certificate.

  • ALLOW_SHA1_HASHING: Permits client certificates signed with the legacy SHA-1 algorithm.

  • ALLOW_EXPIRED_LEAF_CERTIFICATE: Evaluates expired leaf certificates by validating them as of 1 second prior to their actual expiration time.

This feature is available for all Application Load Balancer types.

For more information, see Client validation modes.

Email session hiding (Apps API)

You can now hide email sessions from the agent adapter using two new Apps API endpoints. Hiding a session removes it from agent lists, counts, search, and the supervisor dashboard's live counters without deleting the session or changing its status. If an end-user replies to a hidden session, the session automatically unhides and follows your existing reply-handling rules. This capability is available through the Apps API only.

By default, this capability is inactive. Contact Google Cloud Support to turn it on for your instance.

Fixed

This release addresses the following issues:

  • Fixed an issue where cross-language agent-to-queue voice transfers played whisper audio and displayed Selected Language in the source language instead of the transfer target language.

  • Fixed an issue where the unread chat badge in the agent adapter displayed an inflated count on chats escalated from a virtual agent when real-time redaction was enabled.

  • Fixed an issue where inbound calls with invalid or unformattable caller IDs didn't load for agents, causing calls to loop between agents until the caller hung up.

  • Fixed an issue where the Deflections - Calls dashboard double-counted calls redirected to a phone number.

  • Fixed an issue where call transcripts and SmartActions panels didn't load for blended SMS calls.

  • Fixed an issue where the Salesforce adapter failed to connect without logging an error when loaded in the agent desktop without a required security key.

  • Fixed an issue where warm transfers to a supervisor queue failed silently and looped repeatedly when the receiving agent had microphone permissions disabled.

  • Fixed an issue where the Microsoft 365 mailbox selection dropdown appeared empty during OAuth setup using client credentials when permissions were missing.

  • Fixed an issue where supervisor-initiated sign-outs for in-call agents discarded mandatory call dispositions and didn't record the interaction outcome in reporting.

  • Fixed an issue where the queue list in the CCaaS portal remained in a loading state for an extended period after signing in.

  • Fixed an issue where calls using Nexmo numbers disconnected when attempting pre-session deflection during virtual agent escalation.

  • Fixed an issue where unanswered extension and inbound calls that were abandoned by the caller were missing from the Missed list in the call adapter and were incorrectly classified as unknown errors.

  • Fixed an issue where call transfers didn't requeue immediately when the receiving agent had a microphone or device error.

  • Fixed an issue where after-hours and overcapacity announcement and options messages couldn't be customized at the individual user and team levels.

  • Fixed an issue where certain failed calls appeared as "Failed: ()" in session data exports and were missing from advanced reporting filters.

  • Fixed an issue where virtual agent call recordings weren't exported if a caller hung up immediately after being transferred to a post-session survey.

  • Fixed an issue where custom SIP headers weren't passed on direct inbound calls deflected to a contact list or queue.

  • Fixed an issue where inbound calls experienced delays and periods of silence before the virtual agent welcome prompt.

  • Fixed an issue where call recordings didn't consistently pause and resume when an agent clicked the redaction button multiple times during a single call.

Bigtable

Feature

Bigtable offers conversational analytics, which lets you query you operational data using natural language. This feature is powered by the Conversational Analytics API. This feature is in Preview. For more information, see Conversational analytics for Bigtable overview.

Feature

The QueryData tool lets you query the data in your database using conversational language and build data agents. This feature is available in Preview. For more information, see QueryData tool overview.

Cloud Run

Feature

Cloud Run ephemeral disk is in General Availability (GA). Ephemeral disk allows you to mount a volume that persists only for the duration of your service, job, or worker pool instance.

Cloud SQL for SQL Server

Feature

Cloud SQL for SQL Server now supports read pool autoscaling (GA), which helps you more easily manage your application's workload needs.

This feature automates read pool scale in and scale out operations based on one or both of the following conditions:

  • Allowed CPU usage of the read pool
  • Allowed number of client connections to the read pool

Cloud Storage

Feature

You can pause hard deletions for a bucket when you need more time to restore soft-deleted objects before they're permanently deleted. For more information, see Pause permanent (hard) deletions of soft-deleted objects.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Switch between teams in the mobile app

You can switch between multiple teams in the Gemini Enterprise mobile app without logging out and rescanning the QR code. (Teams were previously called instances.)

When you open a team for the first time, the mobile app saves it to your teams list. Additionally, you can rename teams in the list and you can remove teams from your list.

This feature is generally available (GA). For more information, see Teams in Use the mobile app.

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Feature

AlphaGenome gRPC and unified HTTP serving support

AlphaGenome (alphagenome-004) now supports unified HTTP/2 gRPC streaming and chunked binary protobuf HTTP streaming on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform:

  • Streams compressed binary tensor chunks directly over gRPC on shared endpoints (PredictionService.StreamDirectRawPredict on port 8081) and chunked binary protobuf payloads (proto_b64) over HTTP on dedicated endpoints (streamRawPredict on port 8080) across all seven DnaModelService methods (predict_sequence, predict_interval, predict_variant, score_variant, score_interval, score_ism_variants, and output_metadata) and 11 genomic modalities, reducing latency for 1 MB track predictions.
  • Supports concurrent multi-variant evaluation for in silico saturation mutagenesis (score_ism_variants) without HTTP gateway timeouts.
  • Supports model fold selection (ALL_FOLDS, FOLD_0, FOLD_1, FOLD_2, and FOLD_3) across both gRPC and HTTP clients through the unified alphagenome_cloud_sdk Python SDK.
  • Retains alphagenome-003 in Model Garden for backward compatibility with existing legacy HTTP deployments.

For more information, see the AlphaGenome documentation.

Fixed

The following issues were fixed in 1.35.700-gke.124:

  • Fixed vulnerabilities listed in Vulnerability fixes.
  • Fixed an issue where removing a node from a cluster left behind its local PersistentVolume resources instead of garbage collecting them. This fix applies to Google Distributed Cloud for bare metal local PersistentVolume resources created after upgrading to 1.35.700-gke.124; existing orphaned PersistentVolume resources must be deleted manually.
  • Fixed an issue where resetting or removing a control plane node could remove the wrong etcd or etcd-events member if another control plane node's IP address shared the same prefix (for example, 10.201.0.2 and 10.201.0.26), causing the affected node to become NotReady and stalling cluster upgrades.
  • Improved containerd resilience against state corruption if a node reboots while unpacking container images.
  • Fixed an issue where the periodic configuration drift health check failed with a version not supported error while a cluster upgrade or rollback was in progress.
  • Fixed an issue where audit-proxy retried audit log exports indefinitely on permanent errors, generating excessive audit logging traffic.
  • Fixed an issue where the Kubernetes preflight health check scanned all namespaces in the admin cluster instead of the target cluster's namespace, causing cluster upgrades to fail if an unrelated cluster had stale reconciling resources.

title: Frontend Dogma’s Global RSS Feed Is Now a Paid Feature
description:
TL;DR: Access to Frontend Dogma’s main feed—which features some exclusive content—now requires becoming a Frontend Dogma supporter.

Over the years, Frontend Dogma has become one of the leading sources of frontend development news and tools. Frontend Dogma’s growing archives provide unique access to the history of the wider field of web development.

Providing this service for free is not sustainable, however. Book sales pay for some of the work, but so far, few people acknowledge Frontend Dogma’s value by supporting the project on Open Collective.

Starting today, the global RSS feed (with the 250 newest articles and videos) is a paid feature.

You can secure access by a monthly or yearly contribution.

If you don’t like to support Frontend Dogma, you can still follow Frontend Dogma’s individual topic feeds as well as Frontend Dogma’s social media accounts on Mastodon and Bluesky. These are less convenient and reliable but still workable options to stay up-to-date.

Also, if you want to support Frontend Dogma in a different manner and so that the main feed may be made free again, consider buying Frontend Dogma’s books or contributing to the project on Open Collective. You’re not alone: We do the same for the projects we use and like. Thank you.

To start generating videos, set the model to spacexai/grok-imagine-video-1.5-lite in the AI SDK or in the AI CLI. Chain an image model with Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Lite to create a still and animate it in one flow.

title: Vercel Sandbox creation now returns a ready sandbox
description:
A new Vercel Sandbox is now ready to run commands and read or write files when creation completes.

Sandbox.create() now resolves only after snapshot restoration completes, so the first command or file operation no longer waits for it. Startup errors also reject Sandbox.create() instead of surfacing during that operation.

Snapshot restoration time now counts toward creation instead of the first operation. Creation is about 50 ms longer at p50, with a larger increase possible for uncached snapshots. The total time through the first operation remains the same.

This change applies automatically, with no SDK upgrade or configuration changes required. See the Sandbox.create() documentation for details.

Enable this option only if your Routing Middleware doesn’t read request bodies. Vercel Functions and rewrite targets still receive the body, so you can read and process it there.

title: Microsoft Decision-1 now available on AI Gateway
description:
Decision-1 from Microsoft is now available on AI Gateway. It answers typed questions about text with probabilities, choices, and scores. It can be used to classify support requests, select the next step in a workflow, or assess an AI response against a rubric.

The model can answer yes/no questions, choose among named categories, or score an input against an ordered set of criteria. Multiple questions can share the same input in one request. Choice and score answers include probabilities for each option, so your application can decide when to act or send an uncertain result for review.

title: How Rillet ships 3× faster with AI agents on Vercel
description:
Rillet on Vercel

  • Tripled shipping rate in three months with eve agents deployed on Vercel

  • Two-person team closed 800+ Linear tickets in its first 4 months

  • Builder access via Enterprise Managed Users, SSO, and Directory Sync

  • Ships customer-requested changes to production in as little as two hours

  • Gives every builder access to models through AI Gateway

Rillet is an AI-native enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform. Their AI agents do accounting work inside a real-time general ledger, with human approval and a full audit trail. Rillet serves more than 600 customers working toward a zero-day close, reducing the time needed to close their books at month-end.

A product that helps customers close their books in near real time needs a team that can respond quickly to their requests. Anthony Liang heads Rillet’s two-person frontend team, formed only a few months ago, and leads the push to put agents to work across internal workflows, from shipping customer fixes to reviewing code.

The team builds agents with eve and runs them on Vercel, using Vercel Connect to give them access to Slack and Linear, while AI Gateway routes their model requests.

Standardizing every internal agent on eve

Anthony had been building AI applications since the GPT-3.5 era and had evaluated nearly every agent framework on the market, from the major model providers' SDKs to the open-source ecosystem. Each gave him primitives for the model loop but left him to decide where instructions lived, how tools registered, and how an agent reached Slack and GitHub.

Anthony could make those choices for his own agents, but he wanted conventions everyone at Rillet could follow, including people who had never touched TypeScript.

An agent is a directory

Anthony chose eve, Vercel's open-source agent framework for building, running, and scaling agents that keeps instructions, tools, and skills together in one directory.

People who know what an agent should do can shape its behavior through markdown instructions and skills without writing code, while its tools live in TypeScript files whose names become the API. Once an agent is ready, it can move from a laptop to Vercel without changing how it behaves. Rillet manages all of these deployments in one company-controlled Vercel organization.

Rillet uses Vercel Connect to give its agents access to Slack and Linear through reusable connections the team can attach to the projects that need them. Connect supplies short-lived tokens at runtime and handles refresh through its SDK, keeping long-lived provider secrets out of each application and giving builders fewer credentials to maintain. If a runtime token leaks, its expiration limits how long it can be used.

Anthony's team built a Slack bot that picks up tickets and opens PRs, while others run agents for incident analysis and Linear board management. Shared conventions make that work easier to reuse, and agent building has spread beyond engineering.

Running customer requests through agents, end to end

Before, when a customer would ask for a change, and the request would scatter across a Linear ticket, a Slack thread, and a catch-up conversation with an engineer. By the time anyone had the full context, the fastest part of the job was writing the code.

The person closest to the customer ships the fix

Rillet's customer success team now opens a Chrome extension alongside the Rillet app, highlights what the customer is seeing, and describes the change. The extension's eve agent captures the context and, if the change is safe and well-scoped, hands it to a coding agent that writes the spec, makes the change, and opens a pull request assigned to Anthony. Agents also spin up a browser in a sandbox to test the change and attach screenshots as proof, while Anthony reviews the pull request and merges it. If he requests changes, the agent resumes its session and addresses them.

Rillet's CEO recently posted that the company shipped more in the past few weeks than in the entire first half of 2026, on top of tripling its shipping rate over the prior three months. Rillet’s CPA team ships customer requests through its in-house agent, Nebula, within two hours of the ask. As one of their customers put it, Rillet has "completely ruined my expectations" for how quickly software vendors should make changes.

Using AI Gateway to give every builder every model

As more people at Rillet started building agents, connecting directly to Anthropic and OpenAI meant configuring access to each model provider separately. AI Gateway routes model requests to both through one integration, so builders can add an agent without setting up separate provider connections.

The model is a string

In eve, builders choose the model by setting a string in the agent’s configuration:

Agents deployed on Vercel authenticate to AI Gateway automatically. Builders can try different models for a task by changing the model string, without changing the integration. Usage breakdowns show Anthony which models the team uses and what they cost, helping him track spending and choose models as more people build autonomous agents.

Managing builder access through Enterprise Managed Users

As more people are building agents, Rillet also needs to manage their access to Vercel. With Enterprise Managed Users, builders sign in through Google Workspace single sign-on using company-managed accounts rather than personal ones. Directory Sync adds and removes their access based on assignments in Rillet’s identity provider, so account administration follows the company’s directory.

Rillet set up Enterprise Managed Users on its own and moved builders from personal to company-managed accounts in one transition, bringing their Vercel sign-in and account access under Rillet’s identity provider.

What's next

Anthony is building what Rillet thinks of as its agent factory, so bigger features can follow the same pipeline as small fixes. One agent writes PRDs and technical specs, while another connects to Rillet's Linear boards, Miro diagrams, and knowledge base to give other agents the context they need. With subagents and delegation built into eve, Anthony can add these specialized agents as directories within the same framework.

For a company whose mission is collapsing month-long processes into zero days, building agents in eve and running them on Vercel brings that same focus on speed to its internal tooling.

About Rillet: Rillet is the AI-native ERP built for the era of agentic finance. By combining a real-time general ledger, continuous close architecture, and AI agents in one system, Rillet enables humans and agents to run finance together with full context, controls, and auditability.

title: Findings from the $1M Vercel Sandbox challenge
description:
In August, we launched the $1M hacker challenge for Vercel Sandbox, inviting security researchers to try and escape Vercel Sandbox. We also coordinated with cybersecurity experts Trail of Bits to review the source code and security architecture.

Here is a summary of the challenge:

  • 1,285 reports over two weeks

  • $242,000 in bounties paid out

  • One Linux kernel zeroday vulnerability uncovered

No reports showed anyone accessing customer data in Vercel Sandbox. The most severe finding was the defect in the upstream Linux kernel.

The kernel zero day

The program's most important report arrived on day three.

Paulos Yibelo of pwn.ai, a HackerOne researcher working from a standard sandbox with no special access, found a defect in the Linux kernel's networking stack. Paulos discovered that specially crafted packets sent from within the microVM enabled three different attacks:

  1. Leak host memory over the network

  2. Crash the host machine

  3. Execute code on the host

Leaking host memory

In the first attack, memory from the host, the machine your sandbox shares with other tenants, shows up in packets the guest sends over the internet. This can happen continuously, for as long as the guest keeps sending.

This attack was demonstrated against Vercel production sandboxes.

Crashing the host and executing code on the host

The researcher also found that by sending specific packets, they could compromise the host.

First, by sending two packets, the researcher crashed the host machine, shutting down every sandbox running on it. Second, using the same flaw, they were able to run commands with full administrator privileges on the host, breaking out of the sandbox’s isolation boundary.

The packet-related crash and code execution attacks were demonstrated on the researcher’s own KVM and Firecracker machines matching Vercel Sandbox configuration.

Responsibly disclosing the kernel vulnerability

Almost every major cloud provider isolates customer workloads on this same layer of the Linux kernel, so any defect is shared-infrastructure risk.

Immediately after being notified, we collaborated with the researcher to understand and mitigate the vulnerability, working with AWS and other industry partners to prioritize a fix, and ensuring that Vercel customers and other developers using the kernel were safe.

The researcher also contacted the kernel maintainers and worked with them to create candidate patches. Fixes are under private review and CVEs are pending, so we are not publishing additional details until the patches are public. We are disclosing the existence of the vulnerability because it was separately disclosed in public.

Our approach to pressure-testing Vercel Sandbox

The HackerOne challenge made bounties available to any researcher, but we also extended our program to include internal evaluations and an independent investigation.

Before launching the public bounty, we performed live security assessments internally with full source access and support from the engineers who created and maintain Vercel Sandbox. We also engaged Trail of Bits, bringing on two engineers to evaluate our security architecture.

Not every finding came from the outside. Marcos Hernanz, a Vercel intern, found a cross-tenant data leak in the Linux device-mapper storage layer. This vulnerability let any sandbox read recycled disk blocks from previously deleted sandboxes.

The white-box deep dive

Trail of Bits spent four engineer-weeks inside our source code, with full access to the repositories and two enterprise test teams. They delivered 20 findings, and each was tested, confirmed, and referenced to the exact code.

They also performed an architectural review and concluded that our virtualization boundary is sound. Each sandbox runs on its own Firecracker microVM with a dedicated guest kernel, and the device model is deliberately tiny. No guest shares a running kernel with the host, or with another tenant.

On top of that foundation, they gave us three structural recommendations, which we implemented:

  • Find and eliminate all trust in the guest. Our control plane accepted values returned by software running inside the microVM, and every one of those values is tenant input. Anything that crosses the boundary should be derived server-side or signed with a key the guest cannot reach.

  • One policy, one decider. Egress enforcement was split across subsystems that each parsed the same network policy independently, and they did not always agree. We now use one canonicalization routine per data type, one component per decision, and revalidate connections when policy changes.

  • Assume the next zero day. Keep host and guest kernels up to date, reduce the kernel attack surface via build and runtime configs, disable nested virtualization, and use Firecracker’s jailer to run each microVM process with restricted permissions and isolate it from the rest of the host.

Vercel Sandbox findings

We received 1,285 reports in two weeks. This volume is only possible because researchers now hunt at AI speed.

Here is a breakdown of reports by category:

  • 877 duplicates

  • 319 not applicable

  • 57 valid

  • 32 informative

In our report triage we have validated:

  • 1 Critical finding

  • 5 High findings

  • 9 Medium findings

  • 42 Low findings

  • 32 Informative findings

We have paid out $242,000 in bug bounties.

The medium, Low, and Informative findings are small policy-boundary gaps, like a firewall rule that behaved differently than documented and a field that trusted the guest more than it should.

The most severe finding was the Linux kernel zero day defect, and no reports showed anyone reading a customer’s files, secrets, or application data.

We were most impressed with the heterogeneity of the reports. It was clear that researchers used different setups and have different obsessions. Some clearly know Linux namespaces and steered their agents straight at the kernel boundary. Others went after the network policies, and many went after areas we didn’t think to put on the menu.

That variety is what you're funding with a public challenge. Here's one of the more interesting findings it produced.

Cross-tenant disk snapshot restore (with limits)

Filed on day one of the challenge, this report is our favorite example of why we run a public bug bounty, even after internal assessments and a white-box engagement.

When you snapshot a sandbox, the control plane has to record where the snapshot data landed: {storage_url, size, checksum}. The flaw the researcher found was subtle: that answer came from software running inside the guest, and services running on the host trusted it. That is a trust-boundary violation. The guest is where our customers (and hackers) run untrusted code, so the host can never take its word as authoritative.

The researcher combined a known, documented container-escape primitive with this trust flaw. They intercepted the snapshot response inside their own sandbox and rewrote it, swapping the storage objects of two snapshots belonging to two separate accounts they owned. That meant restoring "your" snapshot materialized the other account's entire filesystem.

The researcher demonstrated that each account could read and modify the other’s files, verified the results using hashes, and preserved the test resources so we could independently reproduce the findings.

The limits of this attack matter. Aiming the swap at a specific victim required knowing that victim's internal snapshot storage key, a random 96-bit identifier the platform generates per snapshot and never exposes through the API. The only place that key appears is inside the victim's own sandbox. The researcher owned both accounts, which is what made the proof possible; there was no demonstrated path for a stranger to target another tenant. We still treated it as a priority fix, because a boundary that depends on a secret staying secret is not a boundary.

Trail of Bits independently flagged the same root cause in their assessment, which told us the finding was real, important, and discoverable from two completely different angles.

The fix shipped within a week, and the control plane now binds every snapshot object to the project that created it and rejects anything else. Snapshot creation moved out of the guest-reachable environment into a host-side service, and storage paths are project-scoped with strictly validated URLs.

Thank you to the research community

We would like to thank every researcher who filed a report, whether their finding was a zero day or a duplicate. Every technique discovered in the challenge informs how we protect the workloads running on Vercel Sandbox.

Thank you also to Trail of Bits for your comprehensive internal investigation and guidance.

Read the original challenge announcement and learn more about Vercel Sandbox in the documentation.

title: AI Gateway logs now show session affinity
description:
AI Gateway logs now have a Sessions view that groups requests into sessions and shows how session affinity routed each one. Each row shows the coding agent or app that ran the session, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, along with its cost, models, providers, and how much of its input was cached across every turn.

Open a session to see its cache hit rate, duration, and path. The path lists each turn with its model and timing, and names the provider serving the session along with any earlier ones. Session affinity sends each turn to the provider that served the one before it, so the provider already has most of the prompt in cache. A session that stays on one provider reads more of each prompt from cache.

Filter sessions by turns, client, model, provider, authentication, or cost. Single-turn sessions are hidden until you clear the minimum turns filter.

Session affinity runs by default on text and chat requests. To group requests yourself, send the same sessionId in providerOptions.gateway, or the same x-session-id header, on every request in a conversation. Requests without one are grouped by a fingerprint of the conversation's opening and appear as fingerprinted sessions.

Read the session affinity documentation for more information on how AI Gateway identifies sessions.
